title: Synthetic traffic & instrumentation-noise detector to reduce alert noise
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: The usage/cost/latency alerting pipeline is increasingly noisy due to bursts from synthetic traffic (internal testing harnesses, partner load tests, automated CI jobs) and instrumentation artifacts (duplicate events, retry storms). These spurious spikes generate high-volume alerts, obscure real customer-facing incidents, and inflate paging costs.

Objective: Implement a real-time detector and post-processor that classifies and filters synthetic/instrumentation-origin spikes before they trigger pager notifications or create high-priority incidents in the Console. The detector should: detect characteristic synthetic patterns, tag or suppress alerts (configurable by project/tenant), and emit explainability metadata for on-call reviewers.

Scope & approach:
- Data sources: streaming metrics (token rate, request rate, latency histograms), ingress metadata (source IP ranges, agent user-agent, API keys flagged as test), job schedules, and known partner CIDR lists.
- Detection model: hybrid rule + ML approach. First-pass deterministic rules for obvious signals (scheduled job tags, CI API keys, internal subnet). Second stage: lightweight anomaly classifier using sliding-window features (request burst shape, entropy of user-agents, KV cache hit ratio divergence) trained on 90 days of labeled synthetic vs production spikes.
- Pipeline changes: add streaming enrichment stage in the metrics ingestion Flink job to attach synthetic-likelihood score and origin tags. Downstream alerting rules will query the enriched stream and include a suppression policy threshold.
- Safety/config: suppression is opt-in per organization and bounded by policy (e.g., never auto-suppress severity=P0 alerts; for P1/P2 only suggested suppression unless opted-in). Provide a dry-run mode to surface would-have-been suppressed alerts in the Console UI.
- Observability: synthetic detector health metrics (precision/recall estimates from sampled feedback), false-suppression counter, and sample of suppressed spikes with explainability fields (top contributing signals).

Acceptance criteria:
1) Streaming enrichment attaches a synthetic_score and origin_tags to >99% of alerts within the pipeline latency SLO.
2) Dry-run mode is enabled by default and shows a <5% false-positive suggestion rate on a validation set.
3) For teams that opt into auto-suppression, alert volume for non-customer impacting spikes reduces by >=45% during a 2-week pilot.
4) Include an on-call view showing suppressed events with human-readable explanations and links to raw traces/dashboards.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- Week 1: Data inventory and rule catalog; collect labeled examples from incident history and CI schedules.
- Week 2-3: Build deterministic rules and Flink enrichment prototype; instrument test pipelines with synthetic flags.
- Week 4: Train and validate lightweight classifier; create metrics and dashboards for evaluation.
- Week 5: Integrate with alerting pipeline (dry-run only), add Console UI dry-run panel and sample viewer.
- Week 6: Pilot with internal teams; gather feedback and tune thresholds.
- Week 7: Ramp to select customers with opt-in auto-suppression and monitor key metrics.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Over-suppression of real customer incidents. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds, P0 exclusions, mandatory dry-run, human-in-the-loop approval for auto-suppress at org-level.
- Risk: Performance impact on ingestion pipeline. Mitigation: keep classifier lightweight (microsecond inference), backpressure testing, and fallback to rules-only if enrichment fails.
- Risk: Data gaps for labeling. Mitigation: seed training with synthetic test job logs and manual labeling by SRE/Prodeng.

- Prototype Flink job branch: https://github.com/redwood/metrics-ingest/tree/feature/synthetic-detector
